chapters.title: Wet Footprints
beats: A night nurse describes the 3:12 doorbell camera alert and the still hooded figure on her porch.
She dismisses it as a prank and deletes the recording, but the alerts keep coming for nine nights.
She comes home at dawn and finds wet bare footprints on the dry porch.
chapters.cliff: The footprints cross the porch and stop at her front door; none lead away.

chapters.title: The Hall Light
beats: She talks to her elderly neighbor Hale, who advises a motion light and a second camera.
She installs both and goes to work.
The new recordings show the figure and, through the open doorway, her hall light switched on.
chapters.cliff: A wrong detail: the hall light is on, and she never leaves it on.

chapters.title: Tomorrow's Date
beats: She notices that every recording carries a date stamp one day ahead.
She tests it by taping a note to her front door.
The next recording shows an answer written on the note in her own handwriting.
chapters.cliff: Reveal: the recordings come from tomorrow and the reply is in her handwriting.

chapters.title: White Gauze
beats: She calls in sick and decides that tomorrow can be changed by not being home.
Packing the car she cuts her left hand on broken glass and bandages it.
At a motel she opens the 3:12 recording.
chapters.cliff: The figure's left hand wears the same white gauze and clips.

chapters.title: The Porch
beats: She drives home and decides to stand where the figure stands.
At 3:12 on the porch her phone shows the live recording from behind her.
A second figure steps out of her open front door and reaches for the bell.
chapters.cliff: She understands the pattern; the story loops back to the nightly ping.
